newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SENIOR CZECH C.BANKER SAYS CROWN OVERVALUED.
newsitem.headline: SENIOR CZECH C.BANKER SAYS CROWN OVERVALUED.

text.p: The Czech crown is currently overvalued and should be at a level closer to the midpoint of its dollar/mark basket, Jiri Pospisil, head of the Czech National Bank's (CNB) monetary department said on Tuesday.
Pospisil, who is also a bank board member, told an economic conference that the central bank was currently mulling the best way to react to the strength of the crown.

"Our starting point is that parity is a base, and this is the right level," Pospisil said. "There is a debate going on at the central bank over the nature of the appreciation of the exchange rate, and on the most suitable way to react to it."
The crown has strengthened by some three percentage points since the beginning of the year. It was fixed at 4.65 percent above its basket midpoint on Tuesday, but eased slightly following the fix.
"The debate has not been finished but our possibilities are clear: either we can react through interest rates or through direct intervention on the market," he said.
Pospisil added that the fact that the central bank had yet to act on the market did not mean that it was not going to.

One of post-Communist Europe's most stable currencies, the crown consistently reached record highs in late January and early February, fuelled by demand brought about from a wave of more than 30 billion crowns in Eurobond issues since the start of the year.
The crown was fixed at 5.51 percent above the basket last Tuesday.
But the market made an about face on Wednesday after the central bank said it has the option of intervening on the market when necessary.
The crown fell over 200 basis points against parity as many London traders bailed out over the next two days. Foreign traders, however, have again started to push the currency higher.
